title: One shape, many orders

job.text: The same receipt shape now has to handle three orders at once. One of them has two items — "a latte and a muffin, nine twenty-five." You still need item · size · price for each, so you can total the prices.

rows: one large oat latte, four fifty
a latte and a muffin, nine twenty-five

naivePrompt: Use the same format for these three orders.
basePrompt: Use the same format for these three orders.

text.plain: When an order has more than one item, make item a list, one entry per item.
text.tech: item should be an array of strings when there are multiple items.

text.plain: Keep the same three fields for every order.
Be careful with orders that have more than one item.

rules.claim: #2 item: ["latte", "muffin"] — with a 'be careful' tacked on.
rules.feedback: You found the move that does the work, but you also kept 'be careful'. It doesn't change the shape — the list is what split the two items. Take it out so you know exactly which part fixed it.
rules.lesson: The list move does the work; 'be careful' just rides along — drop it.

output.source: a list-shaped item field, plus a needless warning

rules.feedback: The shape bends without breaking. A list holds one item or many, so every order fits the same three columns, and order #2's two items each get their own price.
rules.lesson: Design the shape for the hard case, not the easy one.

rules.claim: #2 item: "latte and muffin" — size: regular, price: 9.25.
rules.feedback: One slot, two items. 'Be careful' and 'same shape' didn't give the AI anywhere to put the second item, so it jammed both into one value — and now you can't price them separately.

hints.nudge: What happens when someone orders two things at once?
hints.gap: Order #2 came back as one glued-together value. Which chip lets one field hold more than one thing?
hints.moves: Add Make item a list. 'Be careful' doesn't give the second item anywhere to go.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "same format" → two items glued into one value.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: "make item a list when there's more than one" → every order fits, each item priced.

template.plain: Use this format for all of them. When a field can have more than one value, make it a list so nothing gets glued together.
template.tech: Use these keys for every record. When a field can hold multiple values, make it an array so values aren't concatenated.

notes: ChatGPT: ask for all rows in one table; a cell with "a; b" means it ignored the list.
Copilot in Excel: ask for one row per item so each has its own price.
A chat AI that can't run code: eyeball order #2 — if two items share one cell, re-ask. Never accept "I split them all" without checking.
